results.40 11 12, part 1: audible under the soft pedal; takes of one setting at -53.7 dB
results.40 12 12, part 2: audible under the soft pedal; takes of one setting at -53.3 dB
results.40 13 12, part 3: audible under the soft pedal; takes of one setting at -40.6 dB
results.40 10 12, part 10: inaudible under all three; takes of one setting at -37.3 dB

behaviours.note: Three parts agreeing and the fourth not is what separates a parameter from an artefact, and the fourth is the one that differs for a reason: part 10 powers up as the rhythm part. Two neighbouring offsets were asked in the same runs under the same two pedals and answered nothing on any part, so the soft pedal does not simply make every switch audible.
not_established: Which of the two the soft pedal stimulus was built from carried it. It sends one controller, so the answer names that controller, but whether the offset gates it alone or gates a family it belongs to is a narrower run than this one.

Whether the offset answers on a rhythm part under some other note. Part 10 was asked with the same melodic stimuli every other part got, and a soft pedal on a drum part is a question those notes may simply not carry.
behaviours.reproduced: An earlier pass asked these same five offsets on part 1 with a stimulus that sent a soft pedal together with a portamento, and could measure nothing at all: the glide is a pitch sweep landing differently on every strike, and it took takes of one setting to under a decibel apart. Splitting the pedal out is what made the address answerable, and the split is what the two yardsticks either side of it record.

behaviours.summary: 40 03 and 50 03 each hold thirty bytes a read can reach and they are not the same thirty. A region read starting at 00 reaches offsets 00 and 01 and 03 through 1E; a single-byte read answers at 00 and at 03 through 1F. So 01 comes back only inside a longer read, 1F only when asked on its own, and 02 is reached by neither. A request that spans what it cannot return is answered with fewer bytes than it asked for, and the reply carries only the address it starts at -- so counting up from that start puts every byte after the gap on the address below its own.
behaviours.method: Every start from 00 to 05 asked at every size from 1 to 32, on both blocks, and every start from 40 02 7C to 7F asked at every size from 1 to 40, which is where a request from the block before would have to begin to run into 40 03 02. Each request is asked twice and recorded only where the two replies agree. Reads only; a canary is asked before and after each block.

results.from 00: sizes 1 and 2 answered exactly; size 3 answered nothing at all; sizes 4 to 31 answered one byte short; size 32 answered two short, returning 30
results.from 01 and from 02: no reply at any of the 32 sizes, on either block
results.from 03: sizes 1 to 28 answered exactly; 29 and above answered 28, so a region read from 03 stops at 1E
results.the arithmetic: 00 and 01, then 03 to 1E, is thirty bytes, which is what a request for 32 from 00 returns
results.checksums: every reply that came back verified
results.the two asks: agreed at every one of the 424 shapes

not_established: What 40 03 02 holds, or whether it holds anything. No shape among the 232 asked of each block covers it and is answered exactly, and the four starts at the end of the block before answer nothing at any size, so there is no request left to ask it with.
Whether this is true of any block other than these two. They are the only two the power-on capture found answering short, out of 851 regions.
Why the unit answers this way. The reply is well formed and its checksum verifies, so this is what the unit sends rather than what the path did to it.

behaviours.summary: Type 01 70 does not arrive at the placement its azimuth byte names when the byte is written. It moves there over seconds, passing through other placements on the way, and at some settings goes past the one it was sent to and comes back. Written after a reset, one setting was still moving through a take beginning at 9.6 s and had stopped by one beginning at 14.4 s; another had stopped by 4.8 s. Type 01 71, which carries the same byte at the same address, shows none of it: all 128 of its settings repeat to 0.05 dB or better between takes struck seconds apart. Read after arrival the two types return the same figures -- 31 positions in each of the two output modes, 62 readings, none further apart than 0.03 dB against takes that repeat to 0.01.
behaviours.method: Three runs. The first wrote one byte and then took a series of takes without writing again, which is what separates arriving somewhere from never stopping: a pair of settle times cannot, because both return two numbers. Four blocks -- a setting the earlier sweep repeated to 0.01 dB as the control, two settings it did not, and one of those two repeated with the gap between takes grown from nothing to twelve seconds. A reading that keeps returning the same few values whatever the gap is turning; one that sits where the even-cadence block ended has arrived. The second run swept one setting inside each of the 31 positions in both output modes, waiting ten seconds after each write and then taking three takes, all three kept. The third re-asked every setting whose last two takes were more than 0.05 dB apart -- nine of the sixty-two -- after waiting thirty seconds. Each setting was written after a reset, so the distance travelled is from the same starting placement every time and not from the setting before it.

results.the control: Byte 75, six takes over 24 s: -8.96 to -8.95 dB, spread 0.04. Steady from the first take, so a block that is not steady is not the block's doing.
results.one write, fourteen takes: Byte 1: +3.44, +12.03, +0.85, then +0.10 to +0.14 dB for eleven more takes out to 62 s. It converges and stays.
results.the same write through a growing gap: Byte 1 again, with the gap between takes grown 0 to 12 s: +3.38, +10.23, then +0.12 to +0.15 dB. The same place the even-cadence takes ended at, so the values do not follow the cadence.
results.arrival is not one time: Byte 1 had stopped by a take beginning at 14.4 s; byte 35 by one beginning at 4.8 s.
results.it goes past and comes back: At byte 79 the takes read -2.08, -12.48, then -10.51, and -10.51 is where it stays. The middle value is near what the byte three positions further on reads, so the placement travelled past the one it was sent to. The settings this happens at take longest: seven of the 31 positions in Phones and two in Speaker had not finished after ten seconds, and all nine are on the same side of centre.
results.the other type: Type 01 71 at all 128 settings: no setting spreads more than 0.05 dB between takes, in either output mode.
results.after arrival the two agree: 31 positions in each output mode. Phones and Speaker, 62 readings, largest difference 0.03 dB. The steadiest setting of each run repeats to 0.01 dB, so the agreement is at the floor of what the runs resolve.
results.what keeping the early take costs: The band reading keeps a band only where the separation repeats between a setting's takes, and it measures that over every take of the setting. So a setting whose first take was struck mid-movement loses the whole of its band reading rather than part of it: of 113 twelfth octaves the ten-second sweep kept 0 at seven settings in Phones and between 11 and 32 at eight settings in Speaker, against 89 to 108 everywhere else. The stage refused them on its own and averaged nothing, which is the behaviour wanted -- but it means the witness take has to be paid for in a longer wait before the bands can be read, not merely noted.
results.what a reading taken during it looks lik: The earlier sweep of 01 70 took its takes without waiting, and its published figures miss the arrived ones by up to 20.56 dB in Phones and 10.30 in Speaker. Its two takes at an unarrived setting land near +3 and +12 dB whatever the byte is, because both are points on one journey rather than two readings of one placement.

behaviours.found_by: A sweep whose two takes of one setting disagreed by about nine decibels at most settings and agreed to a hundredth at others, with the disagreeing takes landing in the same two places whatever the byte was.
not_established: What the placement does between takes. The series is sampled about every 4.8 seconds, which is a take, so the path between two takes is not read and no time constant is fitted to it.

Why arrival takes longer at some settings than others. The distance travelled from the reset placement and the overshoot are both consistent with what came back and neither was measured against the other.

Whether writing 0 to the Turn byte does anything. It was held at 0 in every run here, which is the condition the earlier sweep held, so this says what happens under that condition and not what the byte does.

Whether the arrival time depends on where the placement was before the write. Every setting here was written after a reset, which is what makes the runs comparable and also what stops them answering this.
behaviours.reproduced: Three times over, and the third is the one that matters: nine settings the ten-second wait had not reached were re-asked after thirty seconds and all nine landed where the other type reads, the worst of them moving 0.50 dB to get there. Which settings is a rule and not a list -- every one whose takes spread further than the coarsest thing the run resolved -- so what was re-asked could not depend on what the answer would be. The rule was written first over the last two takes rather than over all of them, which named nine settings and left eleven the band reading had already thrown away whole; corrected to the spread the band reading itself keeps a band by, it names fourteen in one output mode and twelve in the other, and those were asked. Taking the last of each setting's three takes instead would have given the same agreement without the run, and was not done: the run declared before it went that the first take is the witness and the two after it the reading, and moving to the last one with the numbers in hand is choosing the statistic that flatters the result.
behaviours.note: The azimuth sweep of 01 70 taken without waiting is not retracted. It is what takes struck at once return, the runs made afterwards are what takes struck after waiting return, and each record carries its own account of which it is. One verdict does not survive the distinction: did_not_repeat_within_a_setting came back true in Phones and false in Speaker, and the same movement produced both -- the widest setting spreads 13.34 dB in one and 9.80 in the other, either side of a bar at 12. Neither is a reading of the byte, and the bar was left where it is rather than moved to suit them.
